ownerStatement: On 21 November 2026 repeat98 answered “Approve this scoped release” for FM Synth 0.1.5 after reviewing the measured MKII results and the open limits. The owner also reported speaking directly with Tim Hastie and receiving his OK for the idle-cost change. On 23 November 2026 repeat98 answered “yes” when asked to re-sign this approval for the current source: the 22 November rework that keeps the rest, drops the frame-prepare path and cuts the silent track’s cost. On 23 November 2026 repeat98 directed that FM Synth’s CPU price be measured again (“measure it on twin 36”) and the measured figure written; this record’s source hash moved with it only because evidence/frame-cost.json now notes the package its readings were taken on.
reason: The current USB package is 791e26c5 (public/octatrack-modules/synth/0.1.5-experimental.mwrm). It differs from the package of 22 November, 8cf43bfb, in one byte, the machine descriptor’s CPU price (reserved[0], 6 to 4). Of 8cf43bfb only the cost was read: on 22 November 2026 the owner’s MKII with the 0.8 development twin dce1d30e recorded evidence/frame-cost.json (rest 0, first 31.3, each 0.5), and on 23 November, with twin 856cbbcf, its CPU price (one track 3.2 points of a frame, priced 4; TESTING.md). On 23 November 2026 791e26c5 itself ran in two rolled-back trials on the owner’s MKII with twin 856cbbcf (TESTING.md): installed on no track it added 0.1 to 0.2 frame points and a pick while it rested was admitted, but a track that had played notes kept costing about 11.4 frame points more than before its first note while silent or stopped, so the released-silence and after-STOP paths did not show their saving (follow-up #2030). Not run on the unit: GLIDE with a LEG MONO sample track, HOLD after a wake, the first note by ear and a legacy FMSYNTH marker project. The MKII results in TESTING.md for the earlier packages b904a852, 2ac17c3a and 5b425a33 are those packages’, not this one’s. Worst-case chip cycles, complete memory bounds, cold-start persistence and sample-locked legacy notes on the unit remain open. UI captures are retained from 0.1.2 because the release keeps the same controls and pages.
